title: Mitchell TTX · HVAA protection
subtitle: Pulse support, ambush alert and decoy LOEs
description: Mitchell 2024 tabletop exercise Figures 6-8: three lines of effort used notional expendable and recoverable CCA in concert with F-22s, F-15EX and E-7A/tanker support to complicate the PLA threat to high-value airborne assets.
assumptions: Mission tasks and platform roles follow Figures 6-8 and page 20 of the February 2025 report; they describe TTX concepts rather than actual flights.
Figures describe broad areas (Ryukyus, mainland Japan, Guam) but provide no verifiable flight-track coordinates, actual launch times or platform-level observed movements.

The report states LOE 2 could launch up to four reactive waves per day depending on target availability and expendable CCA allocation could be exhausted in two days; playback seconds are not those timings.
Map actor positions are fictional study points and do not represent actual E-7A or tanker orbits or adversary engagements.

Additional icons show selected roles described by Figures 6–8, but no source-confirmed aircraft count or actual trajectory. The electronic warfare CCA symbol used here is a category proxy rather than a documented match of a specific design.

phases.title: LOE 1 · Protect Strike-Pulse HVAA
phases.narrative: F-22s and CCA support the HVAA shield and counter notional KJ-500 threats; the report depicts E-7s and refueling aircraft as protected assets.

phases.title: LOE 2 · Ambush Alert
phases.narrative: Reactive expendable counterair waves supported by ISR/EW CCA are considered between pulses, up to four per day depending on target availability (Figure 7).

phases.title: LOE 3 · Decoy and ISR
phases.narrative: Recoverable ISR/EW CCA provide decoy pressure, broad coverage and target-of-opportunity detection between pulses (Figure 8).

phases.title: Reposition / Repeat (Illustrative)
phases.narrative: The report describes initial air-launched and later ground-launched EW CCA from the Ryukyus; the short playback reset is editorial only.
